video_title: Micah Nori Media Availability | Oct. 5, 2026 | Portland Trail Blazers

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori emphasizes defensive rebounding and turnover reduction for the team
quotes.excerpt: the one thing that this team we need to do and focus is the defensive rebounding
quotes.quote: The one thing that this team we need to do and focus is the defensive rebounding and the turnovers. And if we can do those things when we are tired, then we should be able to do them when we are fully energized. So those were the main things we are working on.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the Blazers are prioritizing defensive rebounding and ball security in camp. He notes that if the team can execute these fundamentals while tired, they will be in a good spot when fully energized.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the intensity and shooting development of Scoot Henderson
quotes.excerpt: he brings a lot of intensity. I think that he is working on his shooting
quotes.quote: I think he brings a lot of intensity. I think that he is working on his shooting to make himself even more so of a three-and-D type player and implement that to his game. I think the one thing that you get with Scoot is you know exactly what you are going to get when you put him on the floor every single night.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Scoot Henderson is working to evolve into a three and D type player. Nori praised Henderson for his consistency, stating you know exactly what you are going to get when you put him on the floor every night.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori defines availability and playing hard as essential skills
quotes.excerpt: availability, in my opinion, is a skill. Being available to play and playing hard is a skill
quotes.quote: Availability, in my opinion, is a skill. Being available to play and playing hard is a skill. And if I ever have to or any coach has to coach and encourage to play hard, then most likely we are going to be in trouble. And so far with this group, that is one of the luxuries we have. It is a hard playing team.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori believes availability is a skill. He says that if a coach has to encourage players to play hard, the team is in trouble, but he is pleased that this group is naturally a hard playing team.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Scoot Henderson's role and performance in training camp
quotes.excerpt: he has done nothing in this camp to deter not wanting him on the floor
quotes.quote: He has done nothing in this camp to deter not wanting him on the floor. So he is not playing himself out of that position. He is literally right there. And I think like I said, any coach, when you have the luxury of putting a guy on the floor that is going to get you extra possessions, that is going to do all the dirty things that like the rebounding, the screening, and do things without the ball is a better way to put it, and he is willing to do them.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Scoot Henderson has done nothing in camp to lose his spot. Nori highlighted Henderson's willingness to do the dirty work like rebounding and screening without the ball as a major asset.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Scoot Henderson's shooting mechanics and consistency
quotes.excerpt: I think he can get better shooting. A lot of his stuff is that he doesn't miss left or right
quotes.quote: I think he can get better shooting. A lot of his stuff is that he doesn't miss left or right. You have to worry about guys that are missing left and right. When you miss long and short, you can fix it because that means everything is pretty much online. And luckily for Scoot, if you watch him, he usually just misses short. So that is why I think that he does have a chance. And then obviously see him out here with JT, John Stockton, who is as good as anybody as far as shooting mechanics go, and cleaning that up and consistently working on so he can get better.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori is optimistic about Scoot Henderson's shooting development, noting that his misses are usually short rather than left or right. He says that means his mechanics are online and fixable with repetition.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori notes Scoot Henderson's improved numbers since joining the Blazers
quotes.excerpt: his numbers have gotten drastically better since he stepped foot as a Portland Trail Blazer
quotes.quote: His numbers have gotten drastically better since he stepped foot as a Portland Trail Blazer. And he has been very much more consistent. It is one of those repetition things. But a lot of that starts in my opinion, if you are missing left and right, you are in trouble. That is something mechanical. But if you are missing long and short, that means everything is straight and online. You just got to get it there.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori notes that Scoot Henderson's numbers have improved drastically since joining the Blazers. He attributes the growth to better consistency and the fact that his shooting mechanics are fundamentally sound.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team focus areas: ball security and defensive rebounding
quotes.excerpt: can we be better at what we have put a point of emphasis on? Do we take care of the ball better?
quotes.quote: Can we be better at what we have put a point of emphasis on? Do we take care of the ball better? Do we make sure that we defensive rebound? I am not worried as much about the shooting aspect of it because I think that if we take good shots, that will take care of itself.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says he is not worried about the team's shooting percentage. He believes that if the Blazers focus on taking good shots and cleaning up ball security and defensive rebounding, the offense will take care of itself.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on defensive principles: protecting the paint and weak-side help
quotes.excerpt: we want to protect the paint, so we want to be physical up the floor
quotes.quote: We want to protect the paint, so we want to be physical up the floor. If you are going to be physical up the floor, putting a lot of ball pressure, you are going to get beat. And the thing is that when you get beat, where is that next line of help? So a lot of it is dependent on our bigs being at the rim and then also when the big has to step up, that weak side. So it really is one guy on the ball, but the other four guarding the ball.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori detailed the Blazers defensive philosophy, emphasizing ball pressure and rim protection. He says the system relies on the weak side help being ready whenever the primary defender gets beat.
